title: An insurance letter
description: A health plan says no to paying for a power wheelchair.
paper_text:
BlueRiver Health Plan
P.O. Box 5520, Riverside, CA 92501

October 20, 2026

Maria Lopez
Member ID: BRH-449120
Date of birth: 03/14/1991

NOTICE OF ADVERSE BENEFIT DETERMINATION

Re: Request for Group 2 power wheelchair, captain's chair (HCPCS K0823)
Requesting provider: Dr. Ana Patel
Reference #: UM-2026-118734
Member date of birth on request: 03/14/1961

Dear Maria Lopez,

We reviewed the request for the item listed above. This request is DENIED.

Reason: The documentation submitted does not establish medical necessity per Medical Policy DME-112. Records do not demonstrate that the member's mobility limitation cannot be sufficiently resolved by the use of an optimally configured manual wheelchair or power-operated vehicle (scooter) in the home.

This decision was made by a physician reviewer, M. Grant, MD.

YOUR RIGHT TO APPEAL
You or your authorized representative may file an appeal. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by April 18, 2027). Send a written appeal to the address above or call Member Services. Include a letter of medical necessity from your provider and any records that support your request, such as a mobility evaluation by a physical or occupational therapist.

If waiting could seriously harm your health, you may ask for an expedited (fast) appeal. We will decide an expedited appeal within 72 hours.

You may request free copies of all documents and the medical policy used to make this decision.

Member Services: 1-800-555-0199 (TTY: 711), Monday-Friday, 8 AM-8 PM.

simple.summary: This letter is from your health plan, BlueRiver Health Plan. It says they will not pay for the power wheelchair your doctor asked for. You have the right to appeal.

concerns.issue: Your date of birth is different in 2 places. The top of the letter says 03/14/1991. The part about the request says 03/14/1961.
concerns.why_it_matters: If the request had the wrong date of birth, your records may have been mixed up. That could have affected the decision.
concerns.what_to_do: Call Member Services at 1-800-555-0199 (TTY 711) and ask them to fix it. Tell Dr. Ana Patel's office too.

concerns.issue: Your appeal must reach the plan by April 18, 2027.
concerns.why_it_matters: If you miss this date, you may lose your chance to appeal.
concerns.what_to_do: Put the date on your calendar. Start early, because getting a letter from your doctor can take time.

concerns.issue: The letter says they used Medical Policy DME-112, but the policy is not included.
concerns.why_it_matters: Knowing the rules they used can help you and your doctor write a stronger appeal.
concerns.what_to_do: Ask Member Services for a free copy of the policy and all the documents they used.

key_points: Your health plan said no to paying for a power wheelchair.
They said your records don't show that a manual wheelchair or a scooter can't meet your needs at home.
A doctor who works for the plan, M. Grant, MD, made this decision.
You have the right to appeal. This means asking them to change their decision.
Someone you choose can appeal for you.
If waiting could seriously harm your health, you can ask for a fast appeal. They will decide in 72 hours.
You can ask for free copies of the papers and rules they used.

todos.task: Send your appeal. It must reach BlueRiver Health Plan by this date.
Ask Dr. Ana Patel for a letter of medical necessity to send with your appeal.
Gather records that support your request, like a mobility check by a physical or occupational therapist.
Call Member Services at 1-800-555-0199 (TTY 711) to fix your date of birth or ask questions. They are open Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 8 PM.

questions.question: How do I appeal?
questions.answer: Send a written appeal to BlueRiver Health Plan, P.O. Box 5520, Riverside, CA 92501, or call Member Services at 1-800-555-0199 (TTY 711). Your appeal must reach them by April 18, 2027. Include a letter of medical necessity from your doctor and any records that support your request.

questions.question: Why was my wheelchair denied?
questions.answer: The letter says your records don't show that a manual wheelchair or a scooter can't meet your needs at home. So the plan decided the power wheelchair was not medically necessary, under their Medical Policy DME-112.

questions.question: What is a letter of medical necessity?
questions.answer: It is a letter from your doctor that explains why you need the power wheelchair for your health. Your letter says to send one with your appeal. You can ask Dr. Ana Patel's office for it.
